source_refs.note: Instantaneous Velocity: a main subheading of 14.4 Simple Harmonic Motion and Uniform Circular Motion, its own page (owner 2026-11-04); PDF 26-27.

blocks.text: Considering Fig. 14.6, the line PR is the horizontal component of velocity vₚ of the particle and it is parallel to the diameter AB of the circle. Therefore, as Q vibrates horizontally, so instantaneous velocity of the point Q is horizontal component of velocity vₚ.

blocks.alt: The same circle with diameter BA. At P the velocity vp points along the tangent. Its horizontal component v is drawn from P to R on the vertical diameter, parallel to BA, and an equal arrow v acts on Q along the diameter towards O. The angle between vp and the vertical is theta, and the angle between vp and PR is 90 degrees minus theta.
blocks.caption: Figure 14.6: Velocity of the point P and its horizontal component (original drawing after the textbook's Figure 14.6).

blocks.text: Since vₚ = x₀ω and cos (90 − θ) = sinθ

blocks.title: Interesting Information
blocks.text: The expressions such as time period, displacement, velocity and acceleration which are true for projection of a particle are also applicable for particle moving in a circle.

blocks.title: Book correction
